title: Commercial groups of old: Amos Milburn's honkers at the Howard Theatre
summary: With Hucklebuck Williams at the Howard, Milburn's honking showmen beat their written book, so Paul had them close the books and dance.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah, you see, man, this is the same thing warmed all over again. It's always been ah, ah, ah, those kinds of groups. It's always been. I worked in them, you know. Like, ah, Paul "Hucklebuck" Williams; I played in that band. So, I was around the people Clovers, like the Orioles, the./the, you know, all those different kinds of groups. You know, Amos Milburn's Band you know, all those guys, they don't--
But they have to call themselves jazz right?

They never call--they never called themselves jazz because it's commerical type music, man, it was commercial music and for, and ah, ah, and those guys like ah, I remember an incident, ah, not changing the subject but, ah--we were in the Howard theater in Washington, D.C. OK, I'm with Paul Williams band. Amos Milburn's Band was there. OK, and there was another commercial type band was there. OK, but

but this one band, this one band, Amos Milburn's band, they had two tenor players in this band. Well, these guys was like just, just, just, honk and honk, and they had acts,, you see, it was confusing people,man, make the people, ah, ah make the people excited, you see. One guy would jump on the other guy's back, you see. And, and, and, they would be playing these horns and then they would jump off the stage out there off the stage out there in the audience and the people just go crazy, man. Ok, so it was time for us come on. So we came on, we came on with, you know, our music stands and music and stuff and in uniforms and all dressed up and stuff and we had a pretty nice little book and we, and uh, play our opening number, it was two applause{claps twice} You see, that was the end of that. So, the band needed--Paul said....."Ok, close those books and I want you all to dance!" You know. So, it's show time from now on, man. See, you forget all about art now, see. You forgetting all about...or about the art stuff, that's out. And pick up those books, close them, take those stands down and everybody move on the front line out there, see. Now, ah, ah, it's the same thing warmed all over, man. You got these guys, ah, ah, or man like, like singers today, man, makes me sick on my stomach, you know. I watch television, ah, Superstars, making millions man. People man, look,man, I wouldn't have them people in my front
yard, out there, you know. I'll throw a brick out there...out there in my yard, man. And, you know, they're superstars, man.
